title: Campaign actions recheck permissions; repairs to recovery, restores and purchases
summary: The website and backend received campaign integrity repairs after the Android 1.6.0 release. Installed APK clients retain their own bundled interface and local behavior.
improvements: Campaign actions recheck current membership, restrictions and permissions when they commit.
Interrupted shared actions and conflicting drafts retain scoped recovery and retry protection.
Purchases, reversals and loans preserve financial and inventory integrity.
Validated restores preserve complete campaign records; server-produced deletion backups support fresh, DM-only view-only recovery.
Full shared handouts, paused-player controls and failed chat recovery are retained.

title: Shop locations, name imports and fantasy backgrounds
summary: DMs can organize shops by region, city and area and import location names, campaign records are easier to read, and submenus gained day and night fantasy artwork.
improvements: Campaign screens are better organized, with safer drafts, readable financial and session records, and clearer feedback while an action is pending or interrupted.
Encounters can optionally use the current party, and the journal can summarize confirmed loot receipts.
Recovery verification survives a reload, and My account explains backup copies that did not match.
DMs can create regions, cities, towns and areas, upload player-facing location and shop images, and set where the party is. Players see the shops available where they are.
DMs can import region, city, town, area and shop names from pasted text or TXT, CSV, TSV and JSON files, and review them before importing.
Submenus show matching day or night fantasy backgrounds. Turn them off in Settings → Colors.

title: Maps, property, trade exchanges and music
summary: A new Maps tab, property you can buy and run, seasonal trade exchanges, and optional menu music with DM playlists.
improvements: Optional fantasy menu music and scene ambience, off by default, with separate volumes in Settings → Sound effects.
DMs can build playlists on their device and import their own audio with creator, source and license notes in Campaign tools → Music & Ambience.
Property listings: buy a fantasy estate and receive its deed in your inventory, then give or sell it later.
Property operations: party warehouses, home tenancy, staged construction and upgrades, staff, managers and city post offices, all through DM-approved downtime.
New Maps tab: import map images, place the party, mark shops, NPCs and properties, trade with NPCs and black markets, and track session time.
Campaign trade exchanges with their own stock, prices and seasonal settlement.
A map name typed while its image is still processing is kept, so the map can be saved.
Interrupted shared actions can be resumed or retried instead of being blocked by an old receipt.

title: Resource packs, searchable Library and commodity boards
summary: DMs can import reviewed resource packs, everything in the Library is searchable, and trading has new commodity boards and portrait barter screens.
improvements: Library → Resource packs imports reviewed creatures, items and location, shop and NPC templates. Imported creatures can be added to encounters as editable copies.
Long location, NPC and monster lists have searchable dropdowns, and map icons and records open their exact Library entry.
Maps are easier to read: compact icons by record type, visibility filters, fullscreen, and colored pings that everyone in the room sees.
Characters and NPCs can leave or join the party, keep their own location and start individual downtime. DMs can hide NPC records and sheets.
Market and Trade Exchanges show compact commodity boards with quotes and price charts that lead straight into buying and selling.
Trading & Barter uses portraits, searchable inventory tiles and central offer trays, and fits phones down to 320 px wide.
Global markets open only while the party is in a city, and DMs can import a reviewed list of fantasy commodities.
Market suppliers keep goods and prices correct, reversals stay consistent, and history shows older records with their original values.
Pending work is kept when a shared campaign reply arrives incomplete.

title: Ships, map categories and player Library access
summary: Owned ships and shipyards, map categories with free party placement and combat tiles, and DM control over what players can look up.
improvements: Every city gets one editable default trade exchange. Existing custom exchanges are unchanged.
Players see role-appropriate Library lookups, paused during encounters by default, and DMs can limit or turn them off. Help has separate player and DM guides.
Ships: buy and name ships, store cargo, crew them, request repairs and upgrades and make downtime voyages, with private shipyards and DM teleport.
Maps have categories (regional, city, dungeon, property, wilderness, battle, ship and other) with a type filter, free party placement and combat tiles for encounters and ships.
Initiative rows stay in place while scores are entered, and Sort initiative orders them when the DM chooses.
Links from review requests, holdings and property guidance open the right screen, and DMs get a global market readout.
Mobile character sheets offer Retry after a failed load instead of crashing.

title: Blacksmith commissions and hourly downtime training
summary: Players can commission weapons and armor from a blacksmith, and downtime now has hourly budgets with DM-reviewed NPC training.
improvements: Blacksmith commissions: contribute materials, pay once, wait through DM-approved downtime and collect the finished item at the forge.
Downtime has an hourly budget per character (16 usable hours a day by default), shared by training, property labor and away activities. DMs review NPC training.
Late training bookkeeping can be confirmed against the location and levels at the time.
The selected map icon is highlighted.
NPC records start collapsed, and the creation editor opens above the list.
Shared rooms check for changes more efficiently and no longer re-send an unchanged campaign in full.

title: Player Home opens your sheet on phones, and property pickers scroll again
summary: Player Home, character sheets, recovery and downtime screens are clearer, and pickers scroll properly on phones.
improvements: On a phone, Player Home opens your assigned sheet directly. Sheet export and reload are grouped under Sheet tools, next to a dice shortcut.
The shared status strip offers retry and recovery, and tells a saved turn draft apart from committed campaign changes.
DM readouts, selectors and downtime budget and training groups are easier to read.
Property pickers scroll by touch on phones again.
Property listings offer reviewed ship presets.

title: Player TV display
summary: DMs can show maps, encounters and loot on a TV or second monitor while keeping their own screens open.
improvements: Open a dedicated player display from the header, Maps or the current encounter.
The display shows shared maps with saved grid and token positions, revealed combatants, turns and optional confirmed loot awards, with fullscreen, rotation and fit controls.
Lootsplit can stay open in several tabs or windows at once.

title: Online tabletop for remote players
summary: Remote players can use Maps in their own sessions, with token movement, measurements, fog and protected map media.
improvements: Players move their assigned tokens by dragging, with the keyboard or to an exact position, and can measure distances and place area templates.
DMs control scenes and cameras, saved fog and optional vision, and detailed map media stays hidden from players who should not see it.
DMs can import reviewed Universal VTT (UVTT) maps.
Fullscreen maps fill desktop and phone screens, with floating zoom, Fit map and Ping controls and a scrollable tools drawer.

title: Connected Maps workspace
summary: Maps became one persistent workspace that connects regions, local businesses and encounters, with a less crowded phone layout.
improvements: Move between linked maps with Back and breadcrumbs, and each scene keeps its own camera.
Map pins open the existing shops, smiths, NPCs and properties, and encounters started from a map can be recovered.
Maps settings typed before the first map import are kept.
On portrait phones, Maps has settings beside the title, full-width search and a bottom tool dock.
The website download published Android 1.8.0 and 1.8.1.
The site owner has a private status page in My account. Nothing changes for players or DMs.

title: Security hardening and a redesigned website
summary: Accounts, private rolls and shared rooms were hardened, several reliability bugs were fixed, and the public website was redesigned.
improvements: Security: stronger account protections, better protected private rolls and stricter browser security headers.
Character rolls work again in rooms that use map images or resource packs.
Encounter drafts are no longer replaced by a background reload, a failed campaign deletion no longer locks you out, and failures are reported instead of passing silently.
Property imports no longer look out of date, item weights no longer show long decimals, and device rolls are labeled DEVICE ROLL.
The public website was redesigned with a parchment ledger look, a Features page, real screenshots and phone layouts.
The website download published Android 1.9.0, 1.9.1 and 1.9.2.

title: Split view, NPC barter and party privacy
summary: Two screens in one window, bartering with NPCs in conversation, tighter privacy for balances, and many reliability fixes.
improvements: Split view: open two screens side by side in one window on wide screens.
Barter with NPCs in conversation: make an offer, get a counter-offer, and a Persuasion roll decides the answer. The DM chooses whether they decide each offer or the game rolls.
A DM setting lets party members see the coins of companion NPCs travelling with them (off by default).
Privacy: players no longer receive NPC or exchange treasury balances, and only players whose character is in the party see party members' balances.
When an action fails, the app says so and keeps your input. Retrying never applies a payment, gift or purchase twice.
Offline campaigns buy, sell, give and trade listings exactly like shared rooms, including campaigns with a blacksmith.
Campaigns with long session history keep saving, and a restored campaign keeps its full history.
Shared rooms refresh less often while nothing changes, and party chat keeps what you type right after opening a room.
Security: repeated failed sign-ins are slowed down per email without locking the account, and pages use a stricter Content Security Policy.
Estates: imported listings keep their details, storage accepts exact fits, and DMs can set up operations for an estate bought without them.
The website download published Android 1.9.3.

title: Lootsplit is now Lootsplitter
summary: The app and website were renamed Lootsplitter, with a public support address, a guide for the address change and faster shared maps.
improvements: Lootsplit is now called Lootsplitter across the website, the app and Help. Campaigns, accounts and settings carry over unchanged.
Questions can go to the public support address, support@lootsplitter.com, listed on the website and in Help.
Settings → Moving to the new website address lists unsubmitted shared-room changes in every campaign saved on the device, and names what stays on the device.
Invitation and report links from the Android app open the right address.
Painting fog no longer fills up a shared room: strokes are stored compactly and undo keeps only the changes.
Shared map images are sent once and reused, so big maps update faster.
Maps: Consolidate fog, a message while the DM's device is still updating the map, the alternating 5/10/5 diagonal rule, and screen-reader announcements for token moves, pings and scene changes.
The website download published Android 1.10.0.

title: lootsplitter.com, a new home page and map place cards
summary: The website moved to lootsplitter.com with a refreshed home page and a privacy page, and maps gained place cards, Show on map and a Here sheet, plus even coin splits.
improvements: The website now lives at lootsplitter.com. The old workers.dev address keeps working.
A first visit to lootsplitter.com opens the home page; returning players go straight to the app.
Every public page has its own title and share preview, search engines get a sitemap, and public pages load faster.
The home page says Lootsplitter is 100% free and supported by donations, and adds a maker's note, a promo video and the kobold logo.
A new privacy page explains what stays on your device, what the server stores, cookies and how to delete your account.
Clearer Downloads and navigation, underlined links and a steadier Help page. Changelog and Resources moved to the footer.
Map pins open place cards, and shops, NPCs, properties, listings and exchanges link to Show on map. DMs can place records on the map and use portraits as pins.
The Here sheet on the map lists the shops, people and services where the party is.
Split coins evenly: split a party fund or an encounter's coins between party members in one step.

Services are recorded only: the DM updates hit points, conditions and the rest on the sheet.
Temples show up on the map's Here list and on the shop's place card.
The DM sets up a scribe or alchemist with ready-made prices from the free D&D rules (SRD 5.2.1 or SRD 5.1) or their own.

The DM can pause, resume or cancel an order with a reason.

title: Fairness: who has received what · Online campaign limit · NPC services: stables and coaches
summary: 8 changes for everyone.
improvements: Party → Fairness shows each character's coins, items at their recorded value and total, with how far they are ahead of or behind the party average.
Coin splits from a party fund or an encounter, encounter awards and treasure-pool items count. Purchases, trades, Give, wages, loans, payments and downtime don't.
Tap a character to see the receipts behind their total, newest session first.
Older encounter items that were awarded before values were recorded count as 0 cp and are marked, never guessed.
Everyone travelling with the party sees the party's totals; a player away from the party sees only their own.

When resolving the treasure pool, the DM can choose Favour whoever is behind: Need still comes before Greed, a tied top roll goes to whoever has received least, and round-robin hands items to whoever is furthest behind. The receipt shows the totals used.
New encounter awards now record each item's value on its ledger line, so it counts at the value the DM reviewed.
Start a room and My account show how many online campaigns you host, for example "1 of 2 online campaigns".
At the limit, close or delete one of your online campaigns to free a slot, or keep playing that campaign offline on your device.
Nothing you already host is closed or removed, and account backups do not count toward the limit.
Book stalls for your horses and mules by the night, with feed if you like; the animals stay in your inventory.
A coach booking sends a journey request to the DM with the fare shown.
The fare is charged once when the DM approves departure, and the party travels over approved downtime.
Write to someone your character has met at a place the courier serves, priced by distance.
The letter travels as the DM approves downtime and arrives in your private conversation with that NPC.
If the recipient can't be found, the DM decides whether to deliver it anyway or send it back.
A fence opens their shop's Sell tab while the black market is open, at the fence's buy rate.
A bank opens the loan request with the bank named; the DM starts from that bank's terms.
Ask an agent for hired hands to propose a staff contract for one of the party's properties.
Tailors make clothes over approved downtime; bring your own cloth to pay less.
Choose an item your character carries and ask; nothing is charged while the DM considers it.
When the DM answers, the fee is charged once and the answer arrives in your private conversation with the sage.
The answer can be added to the item's notes, and the item can be renamed.
Agree lessons with a trainer in conversation; nothing is charged when you agree.

title: My account in sections · A shorter changelog · Search everything, and keyboard shortcuts
summary: 52 changes: 29 for everyone, 10 for Dungeon Masters, 5 for players, 2 for the Android app, 6 behind the scenes.
improvements: Campaigns, Characters, Profile, Backups and Support are tabs; Campaigns opens first, and Resume leads each saved campaign's buttons.
Older links to a part of My account still open the right section.
Accounts that only play (no DM campaigns) no longer see the online-campaign hosting count or the DM encounters card; Open DM encounters stays as a short link.
The heading reads "My account" with your name below it.
On the sign-in page, Bug reports moved below the form, and a sign-in error appears right under the form and clears when you switch between Sign in and Create account.
The two newest releases (and the latest Android download) are shown in full.
Older releases show their date and summary line; open one to read every change.
"Jump to an Android version" and a dated list of website releases open the release you pick, and links to a release still work.
Type a few letters, then use the arrow keys and Enter, or tap a result. Players only find what their own screens already show.
Actions such as Award loot, End session, Advance 8 h and New quest open the usual screen or form; nothing happens until you confirm there.
Press ? for the shortcut list: / to search, and g then d, p, m, k or l to jump to the Desk, Party, Maps, Market or Library. Letter shortcuts never fire while you type.
On phones and narrow windows the Tabs & windows button moves into Settings & Management → Appearance, leaving room for the campaign name and the new search button.
Every fold has the same chevron on the right, the same 44 px row to tap and the same keyboard focus ring.
Small details inside a section use a compact row with the chevron first.
Folds still open and close as before, and the exchange board still remembers whether you left it open.
Party, Market, Encounters and the feature screens (Downtime, Bank, Trade Exchanges and the rest) show a small section label, the title and the main action in the same place.
Market's ⋯ menu leads DMs to Trade Exchanges and Shop schedules.

With Show fantasy backgrounds on, the full scene greets your first visit to a screen on this device; later visits, split view and a phone turned sideways use a short band, so the main action stays in the first screen.
With no profiles yet, the page says "Be the first table listed", lists what a profile shows and links to Set up my profile.
The search filters appear once there are profiles to search.
The DM's home screen is called the Desk on the page too (it used to say Campaign control).
Shop Management is now Shop schedules: it sets opening days and restocks, while shops themselves are run from Market.
Downtime is now Time & downtime, for DMs and players alike.
Old links and bookmarks still open the same screens.
The website's Help page opens the Dungeon Master guide; switch to the player guide with one tap.
Links can open a guide directly, for example Help with ?guide=player.
Inside the app, Help still starts on the guide for your seat, and you can switch it.
In phone landscape the section tabs become a 56 px icon rail on the left, and the header slides away while you scroll down and comes back when you scroll up.
The title screen says "Tap to continue" on touch screens and shows "Continue · <campaign> · Session N" for the campaign you last opened on this device.
The Campaigns dialog lists your other campaigns by when you last opened them, with the time and session.
Market starts with "Shops here". The trade exchange is a short summary you can open for the full board, and your device remembers whether you left it open.
A shop page starts with its name, keeper and place. DMs get an Open/Closed switch there, with Counter and Edit tabs below it.
A "Paying from" bar stays in view while you scroll and remembers who last paid at each shop. Only the row you are changing shows its cost and your balance afterward.
DMs can pick "Sell to a character" once and sell each item with one tap.
Shop editing has visible labels and one Save changes bar that reports each part.
Modern dollar estimates are labelled "≈ $… modern". They are off by default for players and stay on for DMs. Show dollars still changes this on any device.
Copper fields in finances, trade exchanges, ships, the blacksmith and property operations show the amount in gold under the field (25000 shows = 250 gp).
Every one of those fields can also take coins such as 2 gp 5 sp through Enter gold, silver or other coins.
Gold amounts of 1,000 or more read with separators, such as 15,727 gp.
Copper is still the saved amount, so nothing about existing campaigns changes.
Phone visitors see a phone screenshot for loot review, party funds, the trade exchange, barter and ships, instead of a shrunken desktop one.
Opening an NPC from Here, a place card or the Market shows that conversation first and moves focus to it; everyone else at the location folds into "Other people here".
One Find an NPC picker searches names, places and descriptions (it replaces the separate record search).
An NPC with nothing to sell no longer shows an empty Inventory heading.
Campaign → Chat shows the conversation directly: a full-height history, the message box above the bottom navigation, and Jump to latest after you scroll up.
Connection & recovery, device backups and manual sharing now appear only on the Room tab.
Each item has one row with its holder, quantity and value, and a ⋯ menu: Edit, Give, Move to pool, Sell to shop and Remove.
Group by holder or category, filter by holder, category or Equipped, and search.
Select several items to give, pool or remove them; each is its own action, and Resume finishes a run interrupted by a reload without repeating anything.
Editing an item uses a Save button instead of saving when you leave the field.
Players see their coins with Give right under Combined wealth, identical items as one row (Potion of healing ×3), and an Equipped chip.
Checkboxes are 24 px with a full-width 44 px row to tap, on Party, shop editing and elsewhere.
Each Party character card has a Permissions… button that opens that character's individual field permissions in a sheet, instead of a long list on the card.
The toast close button is larger, and small links such as ← Market, Open inventory & ledger and Remove account have a 24 px tap target.
View receipt shows the lines the action recorded and the item it created, with a link to it in the inventory.

A DM's shop purchase offers Undo while the message is on screen. It uses the existing ledger void, so the coins, shop stock and items come back exactly once, and it refuses if the items have since moved.
Fields that save when you leave them (account names, stock names, prices and quantities, catalog prices) show a Saved tick.
Features and the home page show phone screenshots below tablet width, so you can read them.
"Everything around the ledger" is a row you move yourself: swipe, scroll or use the arrow buttons. Cards snap into place.
Each card still opens its section of the Features tour.
Dungeon Masters see the encounter's round, turn order and hit points, and can step Previous turn or Next turn; the full tracker is one tap away.
Players in a shared campaign see the round, whose turn it is, the combatants revealed on the map and their own character's hit points, and nothing the DM keeps hidden.
Press I to open or close it.
← Back, in the upper left, opens the map this one belongs to (also Backspace). It only appears when there is a parent map you can see.
X Close map, in the upper right, returns to the screen you opened Maps from.
On Android, Back closes an open panel first, then goes up to the parent map, then closes the map.
A map you open for the first time shows the whole map; phones zoom in only part way, centred on the party.
The map title, buttons and zoom controls now use your theme's colours and the app's fonts in light and dark looks.
Groups: This map, Places & party, Players & display, Exploration, Combat, View, and Shortcuts & help.
Type in the search box to show only the groups that mention it, or jump straight to a group from the row of buttons at the top.
The places on the map, once their own tab, are now in Places & party.
Shortcuts & help lists every map keyboard shortcut.
Tools are grouped: Move, Play, Table and View, with Here and Plan journey now in the same place as everything else.
Tool names show beside the rail the first time; hide them whenever you like, and hover or long-press an icon to see its name and shortcut.
New Layers panel: choose what shows on the map and turn the grid display on or off.
New shortcuts: D draw, J plan a journey, E here, L layers, and I for the DM's encounter controls.
Zoom is now a small pill in the bottom-right corner.
DMs can tie a quest or any objective to a place, an existing map pin, or a radius area drawn on a map, for example "Harkon's horse is somewhere in here".
Draw an area, drag its centre or edge, or type its radius in the map's own units; place it off the real target if you want only a general idea.
The map's Quests tool lists the quests on that map with Show all, Only followed or None; pick one to highlight it and zoom to its pins and areas.
Players see accent diamonds and dashed circles only for what the DM shared: areas for hidden objectives, or under fog, never reach them.
Show on map in the quest log now opens the map on that quest, and Layers can hide quest markers or areas.
DMs: Quests lets you write quests with a giver, a place, objectives, a promised reward and private DM notes, then reveal them to the whole party or chosen characters.
Hidden objectives, DM notes and DM-only chronicle lines never reach players' devices.
Mark objectives done or failed, add chronicle entries stamped with the session and campaign day, and close quests as completed or failed.
Rewards are words plus links to receipts you already paid; writing or closing a quest never moves coins or items.
Players: Home → Quest log shows Active, Done and Failed quests, a Follow pin with Show on map, private notes and a Quest updated notice.
Quests also appear on the DM's Desk, on NPC cards and in the map's Here sheet as Quests here.

Signed-in account requests now count against each account instead of the household's connection, so a DM's open encounter views no longer use up everyone's allowance. Sign-in and recovery attempts keep their existing per-connection limit.
The TV display controls and the map Initiative panel share one encounter update instead of each checking on its own.
The combat status bar and the Initiative panel pause while their tab is hidden and catch up when you return; players' Initiative panels only check while the DM shows combat on that map.
Each combat update now reads the campaign once and no longer downloads map pictures.
Character sheet tabs announce as tabs with the selected one marked; arrow keys move between them.
The shop's "Sell to this shop" picker is named "Item to sell", and Market quotes read out the good, exchange, prices and change.
Gains, losses and "Open for trading" use darker or lighter shades in every theme so they meet 4.5:1 contrast.
The chat history and the shop's inventory totals can be reached and scrolled with the keyboard; new messages are announced.
The fairness "New" badge is readable in the dark theme, and links inside sentences are underlined.
The first Tab on any app screen shows "Skip to content", which jumps past the navigation.
The desktop navigation has one Settings & Management stop instead of two; the gear in the header opens it.
Add loot now labels Name, Value, Quantity, Owner and Category above each field, and its button reads "Add loot".
Shop edit labels the shop name, shopkeeper, location, prices and quantities above each field.
My account opens directly from the website, with its own tab title.
An unknown address shows "This page wandered off" with links to Home, Help and the app, instead of the sign-in screen.
Players now find the party screen as "Party & inventory".
Party tabs no longer wrap, and the pool's count sits inside the Pool tab.
A treasure-pool item nobody has claimed shows "No claims yet" and how many can claim, instead of a list of "Not yet" rows.
Claim all as Pass marks Pass on every item you haven't marked yet; the Need, Greed and Pass buttons stay in place while claims update.
Fairness explains that no loot has been handed out yet instead of showing rows of 0 cp.
Phones and data-saver connections no longer download the promo video until you press play.
On larger screens the video still plays muted on its own, but only once it is on screen.
Pause and play stay available at any time.
On a computer, Session, Party, Funds, Market, Activity and Rolls show as a 3×2 grid of tiles, all visible at once.
On a phone, swipe the cards or tap the dots under them; the duplicate arrow pager is gone.
The Session tile names the current session and has End & start next (or Start session) right at the top.
A new campaign shows "Set up your campaign": add your party, a first place, a shop, a map and your players. Steps tick themselves, and the list can be hidden.
Empty readouts point to a next step ("Plan an encounter") instead of listing zeros.
Duplicate shop makes "<name> (copy)" with the same settings and stock; the original is untouched.
Duplicate on a saved encounter makes a fresh draft with the same combatants and loot, reset to round 1.
Duplicate NPC opens a new NPC form filled from the original; the copy starts with no coins or items.
Review Inbox's type filter and the inventory's Holder, Category and Equipped filters are remembered for each campaign on this device.
The Desk shows "Ready for loot review" for each finished encounter, counts it in Pending reviews, and opens straight to its loot.
Encounters opens your only active battle or loot review directly; otherwise loot reviews are listed first with a badge.
Each item is one short row: name, quantity, value in gold (type 250 or 2 gp 5 sp, with the amount shown below) and recipient. Notes and the exact copper value are under Details.
Tick several items to assign them to someone or send them to the treasure pool at once.
A bar at the bottom keeps the total, who gets what and Transfer loot once in view. Loot is still transferred only once.
The last coin recipient you chose is offered on the next award in that campaign.

Payments, loans, hires, journeys, services, treasure pool claims, training and more share one queue with type chips; empty types fold into a single "Nothing else pending" line, and an empty inbox says All caught up.
Each request shows who asked, what it does, the amount and the balance afterwards. Approve is the gold button; Deny… is outlined and can take a reason, and reasons you use are remembered.
A decided request stays in place as a short Approved or Denied note with a link to its record, so the page no longer jumps.
Approve all payments under an amount you choose, after one confirmation; each payment is still approved and charged once.
Keyboard: A approves, D denies, J and K move between requests. The Desk tab shows how many requests are waiting.
The header shows "Session 12 · day 42"; tap it for End & start next, Session Time and what happened since the last session.
The Desk lists loot awarded, money in and out, requests waiting and characters away since the last session ended.
Pin to Desk at the top of a feature screen adds it to your shortcuts, which then show as a Pinned row on the Desk.
During an encounter, the Desk's party cards have − and + to adjust hit points by one.
On phones, Help and the session chip sit at the top of Settings & Management on every screen.
A bar at the bottom of the tracker stays in reach while you scroll: ◀ Prev, the round and whose turn it is, and Next turn ▶.
Each combatant shows its side with a coloured edge and a mark: ◆ ally, ✕ enemy. The tracker's instructions now sit behind a ? button.
Session Time has +1 h, +4 h, Long rest · 8 h and Next morning. They fill the form; you still review the preview and approve.
Fog brush, rectangle and polygon show Undo, Redo, Reveal all, Conceal all and Consolidate fog next to the tool; Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z undo and redo fog.
Walls & doors and Lights list what is already on the map while you draw.
Combat token and Grid & scale open their own panels; Objects & inspector opens the inspector.
The More map tools button is gone because everything it held now has its own place. Players find the inspector in the tools rail.
Choose a setup tool, click the map, and its panel opens right beside it, instead of inside the long Settings drawer.
After saving, the tool stays ready, so you can drop several markers in a row. Esc closes the panel; Esc again returns to panning.
Entrances can pick their arrival view on the destination map: pan and zoom there, then choose Use this view.
On phones the setup tools sit in a second bar under the title, and search becomes a magnifier icon. Players' phone layout is unchanged.
Every form is still in Settings as before.
A DM edit now sends only the part of the campaign it changed, instead of the whole campaign journal twice; pending edits saved on a device shrink the same way the next time the campaign opens.
Location, shop and other campaign artwork is stored beside the campaign online, like map images already were, so it no longer counts toward the online campaign size limit.
Edits to unrelated parts of the campaign made on two devices no longer conflict with each other.
DMs: View as player lets you pick a character and shows exactly what their device receives, leaving out anything about hidden objectives, people they can't see and places of hidden groups.
Players get a New quest notice when the DM shares a quest with them after the app is open.
Private quest notes are saved under your character who knows the quest.
Removing a campaign from this device also clears its quest follow and updated marks.
The join card reads "Joining The Wayfarers" once your characters are found.
The header's campaign button, the Campaign screen and the browser tab ("Mira · The Wayfarers") show the campaign's name.
My account names each saved membership after its campaign.
A campaign the DM has not named shows as "Shared campaign" and its room code.
Your character opens straight to the sheet, with Home › Character sheet above it; your character library and import wait below, opened from Sheet tools.
When the DM locks editing, a small lock beside Edit sheet says so instead of a banner.
The save bar appears only while you have unsaved edits, so it no longer covers the dice tray.
−1 HP and +1 HP beside your vitals save at once, and Last roll shows your latest result next to Jump to dice tray.
Import into this character moved into Sheet tools.
In a shared room, a character's roll log no longer says it is saved on this device.
Opening a join link finds the room's characters at once; there is no Find characters step.
The join card asks only for your character and your name, and remembers your name for next time.
A missing name or a mistyped room code is explained under the field.
Recovery, backup and file-sharing tools fold into one group until you have joined.
After joining you land on Home with "You're playing …" and a Getting started strip: Sheet, Inventory & coins, Chat.
On Campaign, players see which mode the DM runs the room in; the DM's mode switch and invite instructions stay on the DM's screen.
Get the link, pick your character, play: each step is shown with a short explanation.
The player guide is still one tap away for the details.
When the room is connected and everything is saved, the status card becomes a "● Live" pill in the header (or your turn); select it to open Campaign.
The full status card comes back as soon as the connection drops or changes need attention.
On phones, the scenery above each screen is a thin strip, so content starts higher.
Player Home has a "Since you were away" card: unread messages, treasure-pool items waiting for your claim, the DM's answers to your requests and journeys, and updated quests.
Back closes an open picker, ⋯ menu, sheet or dialog first, then a map panel, and only then goes to the previous screen.
On the first screen with a campaign open, Back shows "Press back again to exit"; a second press within 2 seconds closes the app.
The status-bar icons turn dark on the light themes, so the clock and battery stay readable.
Downloads offers Android 1.14.0 with its checksum; install it over the existing app.

This update brings the quest log (with quests on the map), redesigned map controls, search everywhere, the session chip and Pin to Desk, a faster Review Inbox and loot review, and an Android Back button that closes menus and sheets first.
For the site owner: the home-screen Field monitor now keeps its own sign-in, so it keeps refreshing after you sign out of or back in to the app. Tap Reconnect owner account once after updating.
Field monitor is its own section of My account, with a direct link (/account#field-monitor), on the website and in the Android app.

The top shows the status word, the ✕ critical, ! warning and i info counts (tap one for Diagnostics filtered to it), Needs attention, Recently resolved, a 24-hour traffic chart and plan-usage gauges; the full history stays below.
Copy diagnostics on an expanded item copies a summary for a bug report, without email addresses, tokens or join codes.
A failed refresh says "Last refresh failed" with the reason and a Retry button.
The record that stops a retried action counting twice is now stored beside the campaign instead of inside it, and it is kept for the life of the campaign.
A campaign that had already reached the limit this way saves again on its next change, and the DM can end the session as usual.
Nothing is deleted: every past action stays protected against being applied twice.
If another action lands while a roll is being saved, the roll is prepared again from the new state instead of asking you to reload (up to three tries; the same roll is never saved twice).
Checking whether a campaign has an active encounter now uses an index, instead of looking through every encounter on the site on each update.
Saving a shared campaign no longer re-sends the whole campaign once per signed-in player.
An open map checks for pings every second while pings are flying and every three seconds when the map is quiet; switching back to the tab checks at once.
Pings now check only the room's seats and the one map you're on, with the same rules for who sees what.
Before an action, and when you return to the window, the room is only downloaded again if someone changed it.
Chat notifications to other players are sent after your message is saved, so a slow notification service no longer holds up your table.
During a server hiccup, a failed update check waits and tries again instead of downloading the whole room.
If the table is busy, the server waits a moment and tries again by itself, and your app sends a busy action once more automatically. Nothing is applied twice.
Joining, naming the campaign, switching between Live and turn-based play, managing seats, skipping a turn and ending the session also wait and retry when someone else is acting at the same time.
If an action still cannot be saved, it stays pending on your device as before, ready to retry.
Connect owner account opens a one-year widget session that only the site owner can mint; anyone else gets "forbidden" on that route and on every widget reading.
Disconnect widget revokes that session on the server; app sign-out and account switching leave it running (needs the Android 1.14.0 update).

changes.title: My account in sections
changes.summary: My account now shows one section at a time, starting with your campaigns, and the sign-in form comes first.
items: Campaigns, Characters, Profile, Backups and Support are tabs; Campaigns opens first, and Resume leads each saved campaign's buttons.
Older links to a part of My account still open the right section.
Accounts that only play (no DM campaigns) no longer see the online-campaign hosting count or the DM encounters card; Open DM encounters stays as a short link.
The heading reads "My account" with your name below it.
On the sign-in page, Bug reports moved below the form, and a sign-in error appears right under the form and clears when you switch between Sign in and Create account.

changes.title: A shorter changelog
changes.summary: The Changelog opens on the two newest releases; older ones fold to one line each, with a list to jump to any version.
items: The two newest releases (and the latest Android download) are shown in full.
Older releases show their date and summary line; open one to read every change.
"Jump to an Android version" and a dated list of website releases open the release you pick, and links to a release still work.

changes.title: Search everything, and keyboard shortcuts
changes.summary: A search button in the app header (or Ctrl+K / ⌘K) finds any screen, character, NPC, shop, place, map or item, and opens common jobs like Add loot or New quest.
items: Type a few letters, then use the arrow keys and Enter, or tap a result. Players only find what their own screens already show.
Actions such as Award loot, End session, Advance 8 h and New quest open the usual screen or form; nothing happens until you confirm there.
Press ? for the shortcut list: / to search, and g then d, p, m, k or l to jump to the Desk, Party, Maps, Market or Library. Letter shortcuts never fire while you type.
On phones and narrow windows the Tabs & windows button moves into Settings & Management → Appearance, leaving room for the campaign name and the new search button.

changes.title: One look for folds
changes.summary: Sections that open and close on Downtime, Party, Market and shop pages now share one look.
items: Every fold has the same chevron on the right, the same 44 px row to tap and the same keyboard focus ring.
Small details inside a section use a compact row with the chevron first.
Folds still open and close as before, and the exchange board still remembers whether you left it open.

changes.title: One header style and a shorter scene banner
changes.summary: Main screens share one header, and the scene above each screen shrinks to a short band after your first visit.
items: Party, Market, Encounters and the feature screens (Downtime, Bank, Trade Exchanges and the rest) show a small section label, the title and the main action in the same place.
Market's ⋯ menu leads DMs to Trade Exchanges and Shop schedules.

With Show fantasy backgrounds on, the full scene greets your first visit to a screen on this device; later visits, split view and a phone turned sideways use a short band, so the main action stays in the first screen.

changes.title: Find a group: a clear start
changes.summary: While the directory is new, Find a group explains what a profile shows and invites you to list your table first, instead of showing empty search filters.
items: With no profiles yet, the page says "Be the first table listed", lists what a profile shows and links to Set up my profile.
The search filters appear once there are profiles to search.

changes.title: Desk, Shop schedules and Time & downtime: one name everywhere
changes.summary: A few screens now use the same name everywhere: in the menus, page titles and Help.
items: The DM's home screen is called the Desk on the page too (it used to say Campaign control).
Shop Management is now Shop schedules: it sets opening days and restocks, while shops themselves are run from Market.
Downtime is now Time & downtime, for DMs and players alike.
Old links and bookmarks still open the same screens.

changes.title: Help for players and Dungeon Masters
changes.summary: Help now has a "Guide for: Players | Dungeon Masters" switch, so visitors can read the Dungeon Master guide before signing up.
items: The website's Help page opens the Dungeon Master guide; switch to the player guide with one tap.
Links can open a guide directly, for example Help with ?guide=player.
Inside the app, Help still starts on the guide for your seat, and you can switch it.

changes.title: Phones turned sideways, and a title screen that knows your campaign
changes.summary: On a phone in landscape the app gives most of the screen to the page, and the title screen offers to continue the campaign you last opened.
items: In phone landscape the section tabs become a 56 px icon rail on the left, and the header slides away while you scroll down and comes back when you scroll up.
The title screen says "Tap to continue" on touch screens and shows "Continue · <campaign> · Session N" for the campaign you last opened on this device.
The Campaigns dialog lists your other campaigns by when you last opened them, with the time and session.

changes.title: Market and shop counter
changes.summary: The Market now opens with the shops you can visit, and a shop's counter keeps who is paying in view while you browse.
items: Market starts with "Shops here". The trade exchange is a short summary you can open for the full board, and your device remembers whether you left it open.
A shop page starts with its name, keeper and place. DMs get an Open/Closed switch there, with Counter and Edit tabs below it.
A "Paying from" bar stays in view while you scroll and remembers who last paid at each shop. Only the row you are changing shows its cost and your balance afterward.
DMs can pick "Sell to a character" once and sell each item with one tap.
Shop editing has visible labels and one Save changes bar that reports each part.
Modern dollar estimates are labelled "≈ $… modern". They are off by default for players and stay on for DMs. Show dollars still changes this on any device.

changes.title: Copper amounts show their gold value
changes.summary: Fields that take an amount in copper now show it in gold as you type, and large gold amounts have thousands separators.
items: Copper fields in finances, trade exchanges, ships, the blacksmith and property operations show the amount in gold under the field (25000 shows = 250 gp).
Every one of those fields can also take coins such as 2 gp 5 sp through Enter gold, silver or other coins.
Gold amounts of 1,000 or more read with separators, such as 15,727 gp.
Copper is still the saved amount, so nothing about existing campaigns changes.

changes.title: More readable screenshots on phones
changes.summary: The home page's loot review and the Features tour's party, trade, barter and ships screenshots now have phone-sized versions too.
items: Phone visitors see a phone screenshot for loot review, party funds, the trade exchange, barter and ships, instead of a shrunken desktop one.

changes.title: Talking to NPCs and chatting, without the scrolling
changes.summary: A Talk link opens that NPC's conversation first, and Campaign → Chat now fills the screen.
items: Opening an NPC from Here, a place card or the Market shows that conversation first and moves focus to it; everyone else at the location folds into "Other people here".
One Find an NPC picker searches names, places and descriptions (it replaces the separate record search).
An NPC with nothing to sell no longer shows an empty Inventory heading.
Campaign → Chat shows the conversation directly: a full-height history, the message box above the bottom navigation, and Jump to latest after you scroll up.
Connection & recovery, device backups and manual sharing now appear only on the Room tab.

changes.title: Party inventory in one list
changes.summary: Funds & inventory now lists each item once, with an action menu on every row, and players see their coins and Give at the top.
items: Each item has one row with its holder, quantity and value, and a ⋯ menu: Edit, Give, Move to pool, Sell to shop and Remove.
Group by holder or category, filter by holder, category or Equipped, and search.
Select several items to give, pool or remove them; each is its own action, and Resume finishes a run interrupted by a reload without repeating anything.
Editing an item uses a Save button instead of saving when you leave the field.
Players see their coins with Give right under Combined wealth, identical items as one row (Potion of healing ×3), and an Equipped chip.

changes.title: Bigger checkboxes and a Permissions sheet
changes.summary: Checkboxes are easier to tap, and each character's field permissions open in their own sheet.
items: Checkboxes are 24 px with a full-width 44 px row to tap, on Party, shop editing and elsewhere.
Each Party character card has a Permissions… button that opens that character's individual field permissions in a sheet, instead of a long list on the card.
The toast close button is larger, and small links such as ← Market, Open inventory & ledger and Remove account have a 24 px tap target.

changes.title: View receipt and Undo after money actions
changes.summary: Purchases, sales, transfers, Add loot and encounter awards now confirm with a View receipt button, and a DM's shop purchase can be undone straight from the confirmation.
items: View receipt shows the lines the action recorded and the item it created, with a link to it in the inventory.

A DM's shop purchase offers Undo while the message is on screen. It uses the existing ledger void, so the coins, shop stock and items come back exactly once, and it refuses if the items have since moved.
Fields that save when you leave them (account names, stock names, prices and quantities, catalog prices) show a Saved tick.

changes.title: Readable screenshots on phones
changes.summary: Phone visitors now see phone-sized screenshots of Lootsplitter on the home page and the Features tour, and the home page's area cards no longer scroll by themselves.
items: Features and the home page show phone screenshots below tablet width, so you can read them.
"Everything around the ledger" is a row you move yourself: swipe, scroll or use the arrow buttons. Cards snap into place.
Each card still opens its section of the Features tour.

changes.title: Initiative on the map
changes.summary: An Initiative panel on the map shows the round and turn order without leaving the battle map.
items: Dungeon Masters see the encounter's round, turn order and hit points, and can step Previous turn or Next turn; the full tracker is one tap away.
Players in a shared campaign see the round, whose turn it is, the combatants revealed on the map and their own character's hit points, and nothing the DM keeps hidden.
Press I to open or close it.

changes.title: Map controls: Back to the parent map and X to close
changes.summary: Maps gets a one-button way back to the parent map, a clear X to leave map mode, and controls that follow your theme.
items: ← Back, in the upper left, opens the map this one belongs to (also Backspace). It only appears when there is a parent map you can see.
X Close map, in the upper right, returns to the screen you opened Maps from.
On Android, Back closes an open panel first, then goes up to the parent map, then closes the map.
A map you open for the first time shows the whole map; phones zoom in only part way, centred on the party.
The map title, buttons and zoom controls now use your theme's colours and the app's fonts in light and dark looks.

changes.title: Map settings, grouped and searchable
changes.summary: All map settings is now organised into clear groups with a search box, instead of one long list.
items: Groups: This map, Places & party, Players & display, Exploration, Combat, View, and Shortcuts & help.
Type in the search box to show only the groups that mention it, or jump straight to a group from the row of buttons at the top.
The places on the map, once their own tab, are now in Places & party.
Shortcuts & help lists every map keyboard shortcut.

changes.title: Map tools: a tidy rail on the right
changes.summary: On computers and tablets the map tools now stand in one column on the right instead of a bar across the middle of the map. Phones keep the familiar bottom bar.
items: Tools are grouped: Move, Play, Table and View, with Here and Plan journey now in the same place as everything else.
Tool names show beside the rail the first time; hide them whenever you like, and hover or long-press an icon to see its name and shortcut.
New Layers panel: choose what shows on the map and turn the grid display on or off.
New shortcuts: D draw, J plan a journey, E here, L layers, and I for the DM's encounter controls.
Zoom is now a small pill in the bottom-right corner.

changes.title: Quests on the map
changes.summary: Quests and objectives can point to places, map pins and search areas, and the map has a Quests panel.
items: DMs can tie a quest or any objective to a place, an existing map pin, or a radius area drawn on a map, for example "Harkon's horse is somewhere in here".
Draw an area, drag its centre or edge, or type its radius in the map's own units; place it off the real target if you want only a general idea.
The map's Quests tool lists the quests on that map with Show all, Only followed or None; pick one to highlight it and zoom to its pins and areas.
Players see accent diamonds and dashed circles only for what the DM shared: areas for hidden objectives, or under fog, never reach them.
Show on map in the quest log now opens the map on that quest, and Layers can hide quest markers or areas.

changes.title: Quest log
changes.summary: DMs can write quests and choose who knows about them; players follow them in their own quest log.
items: DMs: Quests lets you write quests with a giver, a place, objectives, a promised reward and private DM notes, then reveal them to the whole party or chosen characters.
Hidden objectives, DM notes and DM-only chronicle lines never reach players' devices.
Mark objectives done or failed, add chronicle entries stamped with the session and campaign day, and close quests as completed or failed.
Rewards are words plus links to receipts you already paid; writing or closing a quest never moves coins or items.
Players: Home → Quest log shows Active, Done and Failed quests, a Follow pin with Show on map, private notes and a Quest updated notice.
Quests also appear on the DM's Desk, on NPC cards and in the map's Here sheet as Quests here.

changes.title: Players on one Wi-Fi are no longer locked out during combat
changes.summary: Players at one table on the same Wi-Fi are no longer locked out of signing in while the DM runs combat, and combat views use less data.
items: Signed-in account requests now count against each account instead of the household's connection, so a DM's open encounter views no longer use up everyone's allowance. Sign-in and recovery attempts keep their existing per-connection limit.
The TV display controls and the map Initiative panel share one encounter update instead of each checking on its own.
The combat status bar and the Initiative panel pause while their tab is hidden and catch up when you return; players' Initiative panels only check while the DM shows combat on that map.
Each combat update now reads the campaign once and no longer downloads map pictures.

changes.title: Accessibility fixes on the sheet, shops, Market and chat
changes.summary: Screen readers, keyboards and low-vision players get correctly announced sheet tabs, named pickers, readable gain and loss colours, and a focusable chat history.
items: Character sheet tabs announce as tabs with the selected one marked; arrow keys move between them.
The shop's "Sell to this shop" picker is named "Item to sell", and Market quotes read out the good, exchange, prices and change.
Gains, losses and "Open for trading" use darker or lighter shades in every theme so they meet 4.5:1 contrast.
The chat history and the shop's inventory totals can be reached and scrolled with the keyboard; new messages are announced.
The fairness "New" badge is readable in the dark theme, and links inside sentences are underlined.

changes.title: Skip to content, and labelled fields in Add loot and shop edit
changes.summary: Keyboard users can skip straight to each screen's content, and the Add loot and shop edit forms label every field.
items: The first Tab on any app screen shows "Skip to content", which jumps past the navigation.
The desktop navigation has one Settings & Management stop instead of two; the gear in the header opens it.
Add loot now labels Name, Value, Quantity, Owner and Category above each field, and its button reads "Add loot".
Shop edit labels the shop name, shopkeeper, location, prices and quantities above each field.

changes.title: Straight to My account, and a proper missing-page screen
changes.summary: Website links to My account no longer stop at the app's "click to continue" title screen, and a broken link now shows a clear "page not found" page.
items: My account opens directly from the website, with its own tab title.
An unknown address shows "This page wandered off" with links to Home, Help and the app, instead of the sign-in screen.

changes.title: Treasure pool and Fairness tidy-up
changes.summary: The party screen is easier to scan: shorter tabs, a calmer treasure pool and a clear message before any loot is shared.
items: Players now find the party screen as "Party & inventory".
Party tabs no longer wrap, and the pool's count sits inside the Pool tab.
A treasure-pool item nobody has claimed shows "No claims yet" and how many can claim, instead of a list of "Not yet" rows.
Claim all as Pass marks Pass on every item you haven't marked yet; the Need, Greed and Pass buttons stay in place while claims update.
Fairness explains that no loot has been handed out yet instead of showing rows of 0 cp.

changes.title: Lighter home page on phones
changes.summary: On phones and with data saver, the home page's promo video now shows its poster and plays only when you tap it.
items: Phones and data-saver connections no longer download the promo video until you press play.
On larger screens the video still plays muted on its own, but only once it is on screen.
Pause and play stay available at any time.

changes.title: A tidier Desk
changes.summary: The Desk's Information cards now fit their content: six tiles side by side on a wide screen, and a swipe strip with dots on a phone. New campaigns get a short setup checklist.
items: On a computer, Session, Party, Funds, Market, Activity and Rolls show as a 3×2 grid of tiles, all visible at once.
On a phone, swipe the cards or tap the dots under them; the duplicate arrow pager is gone.
The Session tile names the current session and has End & start next (or Start session) right at the top.
A new campaign shows "Set up your campaign": add your party, a first place, a shop, a map and your players. Steps tick themselves, and the list can be hidden.
Empty readouts point to a next step ("Plan an encounter") instead of listing zeros.

changes.title: Duplicate shops, encounters and NPCs; filters that stay put
changes.summary: DMs can copy a shop with its stock, an encounter with its loot, or an NPC's setup in one step, and list filters are remembered per campaign.
items: Duplicate shop makes "<name> (copy)" with the same settings and stock; the original is untouched.
Duplicate on a saved encounter makes a fresh draft with the same combatants and loot, reset to round 1.
Duplicate NPC opens a new NPC form filled from the original; the copy starts with no coins or items.
Review Inbox's type filter and the inventory's Holder, Category and Equipped filters are remembered for each campaign on this device.

changes.title: Loot reviews on the Desk and a loot screen that fits a phone
changes.summary: Encounters waiting for their loot now show on the Desk, and the loot review fits on a phone with the transfer button always in reach.
items: The Desk shows "Ready for loot review" for each finished encounter, counts it in Pending reviews, and opens straight to its loot.
Encounters opens your only active battle or loot review directly; otherwise loot reviews are listed first with a badge.
Each item is one short row: name, quantity, value in gold (type 250 or 2 gp 5 sp, with the amount shown below) and recipient. Notes and the exact copper value are under Details.
Tick several items to assign them to someone or send them to the treasure pool at once.
A bar at the bottom keeps the total, who gets what and Transfer loot once in view. Loot is still transferred only once.
The last coin recipient you chose is offered on the next award in that campaign.

changes.title: Review Inbox: one queue, clear decisions
changes.summary: Everything waiting for the DM now sits in one list, oldest first, with a clear Approve and Deny on each request.
items: Payments, loans, hires, journeys, services, treasure pool claims, training and more share one queue with type chips; empty types fold into a single "Nothing else pending" line, and an empty inbox says All caught up.
Each request shows who asked, what it does, the amount and the balance afterwards. Approve is the gold button; Deny… is outlined and can take a reason, and reasons you use are remembered.
A decided request stays in place as a short Approved or Denied note with a link to its record, so the page no longer jumps.
Approve all payments under an amount you choose, after one confirmation; each payment is still approved and charged once.
Keyboard: A approves, D denies, J and K move between requests. The Desk tab shows how many requests are waiting.

changes.title: Session chip, "Since last session" and Pin to Desk
changes.summary: DMs get a session chip in the header, a summary of what happened since the last session, pinned screens on the Desk and quick hit-point buttons during fights.
items: The header shows "Session 12 · day 42"; tap it for End & start next, Session Time and what happened since the last session.
The Desk lists loot awarded, money in and out, requests waiting and characters away since the last session ended.
Pin to Desk at the top of a feature screen adds it to your shortcuts, which then show as a Pinned row on the Desk.
During an encounter, the Desk's party cards have − and + to adjust hit points by one.
On phones, Help and the session chip sit at the top of Settings & Management on every screen.

changes.title: Encounter tracker on phones, and quick Session Time choices
changes.summary: The encounter tracker keeps the turn controls in reach on a phone and shows who is on which side at a glance; Session Time offers one-tap hour choices.
items: A bar at the bottom of the tracker stays in reach while you scroll: ◀ Prev, the round and whose turn it is, and Next turn ▶.
Each combatant shows its side with a coloured edge and a mark: ◆ ally, ✕ enemy. The tracker's instructions now sit behind a ? button.
Session Time has +1 h, +4 h, Long rest · 8 h and Next morning. They fill the form; you still review the preview and approve.

changes.title: Fog, walls, lights and combat setup on the left
changes.summary: The Dungeon Master's fog, walls, lights, combat tokens and grid now sit in the setup rail, each with its options right beside it.
items: Fog brush, rectangle and polygon show Undo, Redo, Reveal all, Conceal all and Consolidate fog next to the tool; Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z undo and redo fog.
Walls & doors and Lights list what is already on the map while you draw.
Combat token and Grid & scale open their own panels; Objects & inspector opens the inspector.
The More map tools button is gone because everything it held now has its own place. Players find the inspector in the tools rail.

changes.title: Map setup tools on the left
changes.summary: Dungeon Masters now place the party, markers, entrances, records and location links from a setup rail on the left of the map, each with its own small panel.
items: Choose a setup tool, click the map, and its panel opens right beside it, instead of inside the long Settings drawer.
After saving, the tool stays ready, so you can drop several markers in a row. Esc closes the panel; Esc again returns to panning.
Entrances can pick their arrival view on the destination map: pan and zoom there, then choose Use this view.
On phones the setup tools sit in a second bar under the title, and search becomes a magnifier icon. Players' phone layout is unchanged.
Every form is still in Settings as before.

changes.title: Large campaigns save online again
changes.summary: DM edits in campaigns with lots of artwork no longer fail with storage-quota, batch-size or campaign-size errors.
items: A DM edit now sends only the part of the campaign it changed, instead of the whole campaign journal twice; pending edits saved on a device shrink the same way the next time the campaign opens.
Location, shop and other campaign artwork is stored beside the campaign online, like map images already were, so it no longer counts toward the online campaign size limit.
Edits to unrelated parts of the campaign made on two devices no longer conflict with each other.

changes.title: Quest log fixes
changes.summary: View as player now shows exactly what a chosen character sees, and new quests announce themselves.
items: DMs: View as player lets you pick a character and shows exactly what their device receives, leaving out anything about hidden objectives, people they can't see and places of hidden groups.
Players get a New quest notice when the DM shares a quest with them after the app is open.
Private quest notes are saved under your character who knows the quest.
Removing a campaign from this device also clears its quest follow and updated marks.

changes.title: Players see their campaign's name
changes.summary: In a shared room, players now see the DM's campaign name instead of "Party overview".
items: The join card reads "Joining The Wayfarers" once your characters are found.
The header's campaign button, the Campaign screen and the browser tab ("Mira · The Wayfarers") show the campaign's name.
My account names each saved membership after its campaign.
A campaign the DM has not named shows as "Shared campaign" and its room code.

changes.title: The character sheet comes first
changes.summary: Players' character sheets open straight to the sheet, with quicker HP changes and the last roll in view.
items: Your character opens straight to the sheet, with Home › Character sheet above it; your character library and import wait below, opened from Sheet tools.
When the DM locks editing, a small lock beside Edit sheet says so instead of a banner.
The save bar appears only while you have unsaved edits, so it no longer covers the dice tray.
−1 HP and +1 HP beside your vitals save at once, and Last roll shows your latest result next to Jump to dice tray.
Import into this character moved into Sheet tools.
In a shared room, a character's roll log no longer says it is saved on this device.

changes.title: Joining a room is quicker
changes.summary: A join link now goes straight to choosing your character, and you start on Home.
items: Opening a join link finds the room's characters at once; there is no Find characters step.
The join card asks only for your character and your name, and remembers your name for next time.

title: 3D dice for the whole table · Item charges keep what you typed · Coins keep their kind when money arrives
summary: 18 changes: 5 for everyone, 11 for Dungeon Masters, 1 for players, 1 for the Android app.
improvements: The DM's screen throws each player's roll within a couple of seconds; opening a campaign never replays old rolls.
A connected TV / player display throws players' rolls for visible characters travelling with the party, and nothing while the display is blanked. The DM's own rolls stay on the DM's screen.
Players still see only their own rolls live.
Turn 3D dice off in Settings → Roll mode.
Uses left is kept whichever field you fill in first; the form still refuses uses left above the maximum.
Transfers, shop sales and approved loans add the new coins on top of the coins already in the purse, as DM payments already did. The total value is unchanged; only the coin mix is kept.

On a device campaign, approving a loan records the same coins and Activity line as a shared room ("Finance: Loan approved"), still leaves the approval note in messages, and is refused past the maximum coin balance.
On a device campaign, a DM payment is held to the same limits as a shared room: a note of at most 500 characters, and no purse above the maximum coin balance.
On a device campaign, editing a purse's coins is refused if they changed after you opened the edit, so an older edit cannot overwrite a newer one.
Giving part of a stack of items with charges gives full items and keeps the partly used one with the giver, the same as a shared-room transfer.
Typing the maximum uses and then the uses left straight away no longer resets the uses left to the maximum.
Choosing what happens when the last use is spent, right after typing, keeps the uses left you entered.
Welcome, Features, Help, Privacy, Updates and the other public pages show their content immediately instead of a campaign access check message first.
Every item in the Catalog shows its icon; a few (such as rubies, harps, keys and cloaks of invisibility) used to show a broken image.
Players' Settings page is now titled Settings, since it holds sound, roll mode and backups.
The "Moving to the new website address" section in Settings matches the sections around it.
Factions can be pinned to the Desk like the other World screens, and its Add a faction form sits in a card.
Creating a room and playing as a signed-out guest no longer make account requests that are bound to be refused.
Add loot, an encounter's loot review and an NPC's inventory each have Charges, attunement & identification, with the same limits as editing an item.
The item is created with these details in one step, and pressing again after a dropped connection never adds it twice.
Players see an item awarded unidentified only by the name, description and value the DM gave it, everywhere it appears.
Items added without these details work exactly as before.
Taking a character out of the party (or hiding them) asks whether to return what they carry. Nothing moves unless the DM chooses; keeping it leaves everything with the character, as before.
The DM picks which items and how many coins go back, to the treasure pool (unclaimed, so the party can mark Need, Greed or Pass) or straight into a party fund.
Everything moves at once or not at all, each item gets a ledger line naming the character, attunements end, and the character's open pool claims are withdrawn and logged.
Fairness totals don't change, unidentified items stay unidentified for players, and a hidden character is never named to the party.
Encounter rolls and loot tables throw their dice when the table uses a standard die (d4 to d20, or d100).
NPC barter checks you ask the server to roll, and the treasure pool's d100s when you resolve an item, are thrown on your screen.
The DM's rolls never reach the TV / player display, so secret checks stay secret.
Players' rolls from account character sheets now reach the DM's screen and the TV display too.
Money in (encounter loot, sales, income, quest rewards, loans, DM grants) and money out (purchases, upkeep and wages, services, travel, repayments, DM deductions) for each session or in-game week.
Money moved between party members and party funds is shown separately and is not counted as in or out; anything that can't be classified is listed, never hidden.
Party net worth (coins and items, unidentified items at the value players are told) with a small chart across sessions.
